text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. Essentially, you are cleaning up the design while keeping the same functionality. The main goal is to make the code more readable and easier to maintain for you and your team. When code is messy or confusing, it often becomes "technical debt"—a kind of burden you carry because you took shortcuts in the past. Over time, this debt slows you down, making it harder to add new features or fix bugs. By regularly refactoring small sections, you pay off that debt and keep your project healthy, ensuring future changes are much smoother and less risky.
